subject: SOC 2 Type II: clarify audit window and request for auth/MFA log slices
messages:
From: Eliot Shaw <security@mednova.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Maya Patel <audits@ravenit.com>
Date: 2027-04-05T09:12:00Z
Subject: SOC 2 Type II materials + request for supplemental auth artifacts

Hi Kimberly,

We're preparing to complete our vendor security assessment for MedNova Health and need to collect your SOC 2 Type II materials and a few supplementary artifacts tied to auth controls (for our auditor). Can you confirm the following and provide an ETA?

1) SOC 2 Type II report and any bridge letter that explains differences between the report period and our review window. Our auditor's target review window is 2026-01-01 to 2026-12-31 — please confirm whether your Type II covers that period or advise the covered dates.

2) Sample slices of authentication events for the period above (or nearest available window) including: MFA event records (success/failure), privileged account session start/stop events, and an extract of access review attestation logs. We don't need raw full-system logs — a time-boxed slice (CSV or similar) with columns for timestamp, user_id (hashed ok), action, factor_type (for MFA), result, source_ip is ideal.

3) A short note on redaction guidance: what fields you consider sensitive and how you typically redact (e.g., user email -> hashed id, IP truncation) so our auditor can accept the slices.

4) Any limitations (e.g., minimum retention, available export formats) and whether some artifacts require an executed DPA/PO or secure transfer mechanism.

If you can get an initial bundle and bridge letter by next Friday (2027-04-09) that would keep us on schedule. I'm copying our auditor, Maya Patel, who may follow up with a small set of schema questions.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call if that helps.

Best,
Eliot Shaw
Director, Information Security
MedNova Health
security@mednova.com

---
Attachment: mednova-request-template.docx (stub)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Eliot Shaw <security@mednova.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-05T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II materials + request for supplemental auth artifacts

Hi Eliot — thanks for the clear ask and timeline. Quick answers up front, then next steps.

- Audit window: Our most recent SOC 2 Type II report covers the period 2026-02-01 through 2027-01-31. We can provide that report plus a bridge letter that maps our control coverage to your auditor's requested 2026 calendar year window.

- Artifacts: We can provide time-boxed CSV slices for MFA events, privileged session events, and access review attestations. We typically hash user identifiers (SHA-256) and truncate IPs to /24 for external sharing; that approach has been acceptable to auditors in the past. If you need a different redaction approach, let me know.

- Formats & delivery: CSV or Parquet is fine. Sensitive artifacts (full auth logs) require an executed DPA and secure transfer (SFTP or secure Drive link). For the sample slices we can deliver via a protected Redwood Drive folder.

Next steps: I'm looping in Vivek (security) and Neha (compliance) to confirm the exact fields we will extract and to propose a sample CSV schema. We'll produce: (a) SOC 2 Type II report PDF, (b) bridge letter explaining audit period alignment, and (c) 3 time-boxed log slices. ETA: preliminary bundle by 2027-04-09, final artifacts by 2027-04-12.

Would you prefer the sample slices keyed by hashed user id or by an anonymized human-readable alias?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0183

Attachment: redwood-soc2-type2-summary.pdf (stub)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Eliot Shaw <security@mednova.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-06T08:47:00Z
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II materials + request for supplemental auth artifacts

Eliot / Kimberly / Neha — adding the technical detail so expectations are aligned.

1) MFA event slice: we'll provide a CSV with the following columns: event_ts (ISO8601), hashed_user_id (SHA-256), auth_action (login|mfa_challenge|mfa_success|mfa_failure|logout), factor (totp|webauthn|sms), result (success|failure), client_ip (truncated /24), device_id (hashed), session_id (opaque). Sample attached (mfa-log-sample.csv) — the sample is time-boxed to a 48-hour window and user identifiers are hashed.

2) Privileged session events: we'll extract entries where role_change=true or privileged_session=true with start_ts/end_ts, actor_hash, target_resource, justification_tag, and session_record_reference (a pointer to our internal session recording; we can provide attestation that recordings exist and a count of sessions if the recordings themselves require extra approvals).

3) Access review attestations: we'll include the audit trail of quarterly attestations (who attested, timestamp, outcome).

4) KV cache/prefix traces: you mentioned interest in cache behavior for prefix-level authorization checks. We can produce lightweight traces that show cache hit/miss for auth decisions (time, hashed_key_prefix, hit|miss) — note these are sampled, not full KV payloads.

Protection & approvals: per Kimberly's note, any dataset that could be re-identified will be shared only after a signed DPA or with an approved transfer method. If MedNova requires the full raw logs for deeper analysis, we'll need a secure ingestion plan and PO.

I'll prepare the CSV export templates and a brief redaction guide for your auditor. Planning to upload the preliminary bundle and the bridge letter to the secure folder by 2027-04-09 EOD. If the auditor needs different field names or extra columns (e.g., user_agent), flag that now.

-Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Security, Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com

Thanks — that level of detail is perfect.

MedNova confirms the 2026 calendar-year window as our primary review window; the bridge letter that maps your February 2026–January 2027 report into our year will be fine. Hashed identifiers and /24 IP truncation are acceptable.

Maya (auditor) — if the provided CSV columns look fine to you, we'll accept the preliminary bundle on 2027-04-09. If you need any tweaks to the fields (e.g., include user_agent or geolocation fields), please reply by end of day tomorrow so Redwood can adjust.

Kimberly/Vivek — one request: can the bridge letter explicitly state whether any control changes occurred mid-2026 that affect MFA or privileged access flows? Our auditor will flag mid-period changes as part of the SOC mapping.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — a short call Tuesday afternoon (2027-04-12) would also help finalize the transfer mechanism.

Best,
Eliot Shaw

MedNova Health
